# The claim responder counts a pull request inside a contributor's fork as a hold

## Context

From Ada's defect-note `a8c88df9` (2026-10-05). On #19230 a first-time Hacktoberfest claimant, `Saadanjum01`, got the reply "This one is taken: #1 is open for it." That `#1` was `Saadanjum0/neo#1`, a draft pull request inside a fork, whose base is `Saadanjum0/neo:dev`. Ada corrected the reply on the thread and assigned the issue.

## The Problem

`.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml` reads the issue's `closedByPullRequestsReferences` and passes every open one as `{number, author}`. `buildScripts/util/claimResponse.mjs#holders` then counts each as a hold, unless the claimant authored it. A pull request inside a fork that mentions the issue is not a pull request into this repository, but it is counted anyway. It is also printed as a bare `#1`, which here names an unrelated pull request.

## The Fix

- The workflow also reads the pull request's `repository { nameWithOwner }`, which is its base repository, and passes it on.
- `holders` counts an open pull request only when its repository is the one the reply is for, which it reads from `repoUrl`. A pull request from a fork into this repository still counts, because its base is this repository.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A pull request inside a fork holds nothing, so the claimant is first in line. A spec arm reproduces #19230's shape.
- [ ] A pull request into this repository still holds the issue (the existing arms, now passing `repository`).
- [ ] The workflow passes each pull request's repository.

## Out of Scope

- Wording of the reply.
